readings: For each location, consider every event, including events that have no budget lines. For each event, compute the average of (spent − amount) / amount over its budget lines. Lines with amount = 0 give no ratio and are ignored, so an event with no usable lines has a NULL ratio. Rank events within each location by this average from highest to lowest, with NULL-ratio events last. Tied events share a rank and the next rank is skipped (RANK). Return all events with rank ≤ 3 (ties at rank 3 may give more than 3 rows), showing event id, location, average ratio and rank.

For each location, consider only events that have at least one budget line. For each such event, compute the average of (spent − amount) / amount over its budget lines. Lines with amount = 0 give no ratio and are ignored, so an event whose lines all have amount 0 has a NULL ratio. Events with no budget lines at all are excluded. Rank events within each location by this average from highest to lowest, with NULL-ratio events last. Tied events share a rank and the next rank is skipped (RANK). Return all events with rank ≤ 3 (ties at rank 3 may give more than 3 rows), showing event id, location, average ratio and rank.
queries:
WITH ev AS (
    SELECT e.event_id, e.location,
           AVG(CASE WHEN b.amount <> 0 THEN (b.spent - b.amount) * 1.0 / b.amount END) AS avg_ratio
    FROM event e
    LEFT JOIN budget b ON b.link_to_event = e.event_id
    GROUP BY e.event_id, e.location
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT event_id, location, avg_ratio,
           RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY location ORDER BY avg_ratio IS NULL, avg_ratio DESC) AS rnk
    FROM ev
)
SELECT event_id, location, avg_ratio, rnk
FROM ranked
WHERE rnk <= 3;
